hits.title: Definitions
hits.text: "Employer" means the Developer. "Engineer" means the person appointed by the Employer to administer the Contract. "Variation" means any change to the Works instructed by the Engineer under Clause 13.

hits.title: Preliminaries and Overheads
hits.text: The rates in the Bill of Quantities are deemed to include all preliminaries, overheads and profit. No percentage addition for preliminaries or overheads shall be made to the valuation of any Variation.

hits.title: Valuation of Variations
hits.text: Variations shall be valued by measurement of the change in quantities, using the rates in the Bill of Quantities where the work is of similar character and executed under similar conditions. New rates shall be agreed only where no similar item exists.

hits.title: Contractor's Claims and Notices
hits.text: If the Contractor considers itself entitled to additional payment or extension of time, it shall give notice to the Engineer within 28 days of becoming aware of the event, describing the event and the entitlement claimed.

hits.title: Scope of the Works
hits.text: The Works comprise roads, utilities, landscaping and a boundary wall as shown on the Drawings listed in Appendix A. The boundary wall shall be 2.0 m high above finished ground level as shown on Drawing L-201 Revision B. Structural design of the Works is the responsibility of the Employer's design consultant.

hits.title: Time-Related Costs
hits.text: Where an extension of time is granted, the Contractor shall be paid time-related costs at the rate of AED 2,500 per working day of extension granted. No other time-related costs shall be payable.

hits.title: Extension of Time for Completion
hits.text: The Contractor shall be entitled to an extension of the Time for Completion only if, and to the extent that, completion is or will be delayed by a Variation. The extension shall be assessed on the current programme by reference to the critical path, taking account of available float.

hits.title: Acceleration
hits.text: The Employer may instruct the Contractor to accelerate the Works by adding resources. The Contractor shall be paid the additional crew costs in Appendix D: AED 3,000 mobilisation per additional crew per activity and AED 1,800 per crew per working day. No more than one additional crew may work on any single activity due to site access constraints.

hits.title: Unforeseeable Physical Conditions
hits.text: Where the Contractor encounters adverse physical conditions which could not reasonably have been foreseen, the Contractor shall give notice to the Engineer as soon as practicable.

hits.title: Right to Vary
hits.text: The Engineer may instruct Variations at any time before completion, including by issuing a revised drawing. Each Variation shall be confirmed by a Variation Instruction.

args.content: This is a valid Variation if instructed by the Engineer, because clause 13.1 allows Variations by revised drawing and clause 1.1 defines a Variation as a change instructed under clause 13. The change is valued under clause 13.3 by measurement of the change in quantities using BOQ rates where the work is of similar character and under similar conditions. The road layers have BOQ rates and the cost agent has priced them at AED 100,440.0 [F-0168]. The kerb removal and re-laying has no BOQ rate, so a new rate is needed under clause 13.3; clause 13.4 also bars any percentage addition for preliminaries or overheads. If the change delays completion, clause 8.4 says EOT is only to the extent completion is delayed by the Variation, assessed on the current programme by critical path and float. Any granted EOT attracts AED 2,500 [F-0426] per working day under clause 8.5, and no other time-related costs are payable. Acceleration is separate: clause 8.6 allows Employer-instructed acceleration with crew costs of AED 3,000 [F-0429] mobilisation per additional crew per activity and AED 1,800 [F-0430] per crew per working day. Notice must be given within 28 [F-0427] days under clause 20.1. Design responsibility remains with the Employer’s design consultant for structural design under clause 4.1; this road widening does not itself raise a structural design responsibility question, but the kerb detail and any revised drawing should be checked under clause 13.1.

args.content: The change adds duration to five road activities: A100, A110, A120, A140 and A150, each by 1 [F-0171] [F-0177] [F-0183] [F-0192] [F-0198] working day, for a total of 5 [F-0203] working days. On the changed programme, completion moves to 2027-02-09 [F-0205] at working day 92 [F-0204]. The critical path runs through the road sequence, including A100 to A150, then A240, A900 and A910 [F-0205]. The contract basis is clause 8.4 for EOT, clause 8.5 for time-related costs at AED 2,500 [F-0463] per working day, and clause 20.1 for 28 [F-0464]-day notice; acceleration is only under clause 8.6. One eligible recovery option is OPT-A100-A110-A120: it brings completion back to 2027-01-27 [F-0475], with no delay [F-0476], but costs AED 145,440.0 [F-0480] and leaves contingency at AED -80,440.0 [F-0482]. On the current facts, I would protect completion date and not recommend acceleration unless the Employer values the buffer more than the cost.
